::: {.eyebrow}
CDSeq2 • User guide & reproducible research
:::

::: {.lead}
Estimate cell-type expression for each individual. Prioritize the gene–cell-type profiles that are better supported. Connect those profiles to phenotypes and genetic variation.
:::

::: {.start-links}
[Run the tutorial](chapters/quickstart.qmd)
[Reproduce the paper](chapters/reproduce.qmd)
:::

CDSeq2 combines reference-based bulk RNA-sequencing deconvolution with optional gene-type prioritization. It returns RNA fractions and individual-level expression estimates, then uses a trained six-feature model to help identify profiles likely to have higher across-donor recovery.

::: {.workflow-strip}
::: {}
**01 / Supply counts**

Bulk tissue counts and an annotated single-cell or single-nucleus reference.
:::
::: {}
**02 / Infer & prioritize**

Individual-level expression, RNA fractions and optional profile scores.
:::
::: {}
**03 / Investigate variation**

Continuous-phenotype associations and cell-type-specific eQTL candidates.
:::
:::

## What the comparison means

The paper compares **standard BayesPrism**, **CDSeq2 (without gene-type prioritization)** and **CDSeq2 (with gene-type prioritization)**. The two CDSeq2 workflows share the same expression estimates. Prioritization adds a ranked subset for focused analysis and follow-up; it does not refit those estimates. BayesPrism uses its documented input preprocessing and no output ranking.

This edition accompanies manuscript version 16. The book includes all **7 main figures, 18 supplementary figures and 42 supplementary tables**, with scripts and source mappings. The tutorial is fully synthetic; its output is a teaching example, separate from the paper's benchmarks.
